Star Energy Geothermal Wayang Windu Ltd Insolvency Puts Operations in Jeopardy

Star Energy Geothermal Wayang Windu Ltd, a key player in the electric utilities sector based in the British Virgin Islands, has entered insolvency proceedings, throwing the future of its geothermal operations into uncertainty. The company, which manages one of the region’s largest geothermal power facilities, confirmed late Monday that it was unable to meet its financial obligations and has begun formal administration.

The insolvency process is already impacting the company’s daily operations. According to a statement released by interim administrator Gabrielle Tan, “Our immediate focus is on maintaining essential services and ensuring employee safety, while we assess the company’s financial position and explore all available options.” Tan added that, while the geothermal plant remains operational, several maintenance projects have been postponed.

Industry analysts estimate that the Wayang Windu facility accounts for approximately 15% of the local electricity supply, making the situation particularly sensitive for regional energy stability. “Any prolonged disruption could have a ripple effect on both the grid and local industries,” said Andrew Holt, an energy sector analyst at Blue Ridge Advisory.

Star Energy Geothermal Wayang Windu Ltd employs over 200 staff at its plant and supporting offices. The Geothermal Workers Union has voiced concern over job security, calling for transparency from administrators. “Our members are anxious about the future of their livelihoods,” stated union chairperson Rita Pradana.

The British Virgin Islands Energy Authority has indicated it is monitoring the situation closely. In a brief statement, the regulator said, “We are in communication with the administrators to safeguard continuity of supply for consumers.”

As the insolvency proceedings continue, uncertainty surrounds the future ownership and operation of the geothermal plant. Administrators are evaluating restructuring options and potential asset sales, but at present, the company’s operational and financial challenges remain unresolved.
